study.question: Does preserving within-slot pairing of event content and historical feedback improve the small zero-start residual gain, beyond factorized products and count shrinkage separately, under the frozen 100-event protocol? Observed limitation: _residual_features in g2-r0008-residual_count multiplies a group mean key by an interpolated task frequency. Two histories with identical group mean content and task fractions but different content-feedback pairing give identical residual features. The existing backbone still sees action embeddings, so this is a limitation of the extra residual path, not proof the whole model lacks pairing information.
study.hypothesis: A count-shrunk event-feedback joint moment can recover complementary within-group content-feedback association without adding parameters or changing the successful relation-content backbone. Evidence is preliminary: g2-r0008-residual_count macro AUC 0.8280519963 versus entry 0.8275704846 (+0.0004815118), fixed 0.8279178190 (+0.0001341773 count-minus-fixed), marginal 0.8279303770 and content 0.8276346488. Fixed has slightly better macro Logloss (0.0547906822 versus count 0.0548190814). Count source g2-r0004-count_shrink has lower macro AUC 0.8272805337 but better buy AUC 0.8970811065 than residual_count 0.8947999887. Thus count reliability and universal task improvement are not established. Earlier direct fusion g2-r0006-relation_count (0.8271699021) and aligned early/late g2-r0007 (0.8255833650/0.8245006440) failed to beat entry, motivating a change confined to the residual path. Those unsuccessful implementations remain counterevidence, not missing executions.

nearest_work.difference: Immediate parent. Retain its entire backbone, products, raw fractions, counts, map and head; add alpha times centered event-content/feedback covariance in the same 8x4x8 moment columns. No added capacity.

Inherit exclusive target category/brand by recency grouping and n/(n+4) local/global interpolation through the parent. Source uses mean-content times task rate, not the proposed centered within-slot event pairing. Still compare source predictive quality and measured cost; no claim the larger backbone is equally efficient.
Inherited relation-content backbone remains intact. New coupling only changes the separate residual features, rather than rewriting these tokens as in the negative prior fusion trajectories.

nearest_work.difference: DIN provides target-dependent unnormalized local activation. That baseline/backbone mechanism is inherited, not newly claimed; the experiment changes uniform grouped task-feedback moments in a separate correction path. This four-task adaptation is not exact paper reproduction.

Pinned benchmark code already pools task-mask-conditioned event projections into task sequence hubs. Event-feedback pairing itself is therefore not a novelty claim. Proposed scope is centered within exclusive target/recency groups, interpolated in a zero-start correction with a shared map and unchanged backbone, rather than layer-wise hub aggregation/broadcast. Original INFNet full text is unavailable through the authorized registry; benchmark code is not proof of exact original-method equivalence.

Cached section 2.3 supplies nearest unified-model context (INFNet hubs, EST feature-specific cross-attention, HyFormer repeated global summaries). This suite introduces none of those whole-stack replacements. Originality remains unverified; a bounded search and implementation difference do not establish priority.

inherited_components: All architectural components and initialization sequence of g2-r0008-residual_count, including zero-initialized last residual layer
Relation-content representation and explicit relation counts from g0-r0003-relation_content_counts
Category/brand x old/recent grouping and count shrinkage from g2-r0004-count_shrink through the immediate parent
Existing frozen host preprocessing, masks, scoring, loss and training recipe; no loss hook or protocol edits
study.proposed_difference: Let n be group occupancy, f its raw task fraction, g the visible-user task background, mu=W(mean x), and alpha=n/(n+4) or 1/2. Original moment is mu*(alpha*f+(1-alpha)*g). Project each visible event through the SAME bias-free map and compute c=mean((W x)*y)-mean(W x)*f with FP32 accumulation and all-event group denominator. Replace the moment by original+alpha*c, leaving original raw fraction/count columns. In exact arithmetic this is alpha*mean((W x)*y)+(1-alpha)*mu*g; BF16 reassociation requires validation. The factorized control computes c identically but multiplies it by zero. Both grouping and covariance ignore invalid positions; zero-length histories return zero and the inherited head output is gated off for empty histories. All four files share parameter tensors, module constructor/order, dimensions and operation shapes, differing only in two literal config values.
predictions: Primary prediction: joint_count validation macro AUC exceeds product_count and both imported source bests; record absolute deltas versus parent, entry and DIN and all four task AUC/Logloss changes. No undeclared task veto or cherry-picked task mean.

Pairing main effect: joint_count-product_count and joint_fixed-product_fixed are positive; covariance values distinguish equal-marginal different-pairing histories. If only one pairing contrast improves, report the interaction rather than a general pairing benefit.

Shrinkage prediction, evaluated separately: joint_count-joint_fixed is positive, particularly in pre-existing history_1_16 versus long-history slices. Factorial interaction is (joint_count-product_count)-(joint_fixed-product_fixed). A nonpositive interaction does not refute a pairing main effect, but offers no support for synergy with count shrinkage.

Parameter counts are equal at expected 32,964,809; covariance execution costs more than the archived product path despite no added parameters. Report train/inference wall time, batch latency, peak memory and quality-cost position versus both original sources. Equal data-pass contrasts isolate the representation; no equal-compute efficiency claim follows automatically.

Host shared-state gates: zero covariance coupling reproduces archived product outputs (predeclared tolerances: FP32 atol=1e-7/rtol=1e-6; BF16 atol=1e-4/rtol=1e-3, with discrepancies investigated before scoring). All four outputs initially match the archived parent with identical common state because its last residual layer is zero. Constant within-slot content or constant feedback gives zero covariance; singleton slots do too. Count and fixed joint moments coincide when every occupied slot has n=4; for a single occupied group local/global rates coincide, but joint covariance weights can still differ unless n=4 or covariance is zero. Host must verify four [B,1] finite probabilities, finite BCE/backward and all parameter gradients (new map gradients can be zero at zero-head initialization; test sensitivity also with a copied nonzero test head), FP32 and BF16, empty/zero-length/no-match histories, eval and cloned-state train invariance to masked IDs/actions/task masks and target action, and sensitivity to visible event-feedback pairing. These full-model checks have not run locally.
falsifiers: Joint variants fail to improve their paired factorized controls, or any gain vanishes in authorized paired repetitions/user-cluster uncertainty checks. A single success remains a local observation.

Joint_count does not exceed the stronger source g0-r0003-relation_content_counts on full validation macro AUC; then the tested combination has not achieved the topic objective even if it beats a weaker control.

Fixed performs as well or better than count within joint moments across repetitions: no support for count-dependent reliability in this implementation. The previous fixed Logloss advantage is retained as counterevidence.

Matched-operation factorized arms fail shared-state equivalence with archived product models beyond declared BF16 numerical tolerance: debug before interpreting performance; arithmetic drift confounds the contrast.

Constant-content/feedback, padded IDs/actions/task masks, empty-history, output-shape/finiteness or gradients fail authorized host preflight: this is implementation failure, not scientific refutation.
Any quality gain comes at an unjustified measured cost relative to source frontiers: report added predictive utility separately from efficiency, and reject an efficiency claim.
alternative_explanations: Single-seed selection noise, rare-label variance, repeated-user dependence and validation winner selection
A different gradient path through shared embeddings/map, rather than stable content-feedback semantics
Covariance noise in small slots; total occupancy n is not a calibrated effective sample size for each rare feedback task
Core action embeddings may already encode the same association, making the additional moments redundant
BF16 projection/aggregation ordering and runtime kernel differences, controlled by common operation shapes and archived shared-state checks
OOV or missing encoded IDs can collide in target equality; recent means ordinal last 16 positions, not elapsed time

Inherited official_offline action visibility and publisher snapshot/vocabulary assumptions limit production point-in-time claims; auxiliary labels are user/category/brand 24h matches, not advertisement-specific conversions
